records.title: Digital Signal Processing
records.summary: Covers discrete-time signals, Fourier transforms, and the design of digital filters.
records.learning_note: Use the Fourier transform to diagnose spectral interference before designing a filter.
records.first_activity: Plot the frequency spectrum of two sampled tones before and after applying a low-pass filter.

records.title: Digital Communications Systems
records.summary: Studies digital modulation, receivers, and communication over channels with noise and intersymbol interference.
records.learning_note: Model how noise affects receiver decisions in a digital link.
records.first_activity: Simulate a simple digital link and plot the fraction of incorrect symbols as noise increases.

records.title: Automatic Control
records.summary: Introduces time- and frequency-domain models for linear feedback systems, stability, and controller design.
records.learning_note: Relate a robot's motor response to feedback, stability, and the choice of controller gain.
records.first_activity: Plot a simulated DC motor speed step response at two different controller gains.

records.title: Digital Control Systems
records.summary: Models and designs discrete controllers using sampled signals, z-transforms, stability analysis, and microprocessors.
records.learning_note: Connect sampled sensor readings and software timing to a digital controller's response.
records.first_activity: Compare the same simulated motor controller using two sampling intervals.

records.title: Computer Networking
records.summary: Examines computer networks and distributed systems, including routing, end-to-end protocols, and congestion control.
records.learning_note: Explore how packets move once a link can carry signals. This complements the physical-layer work in ECE communications.
records.first_activity: Draw how a packet crosses a wireless link and a router, then explain the job of each layer.

records.title: Geometric Algorithms
records.summary: Studies methods for computing with geometric objects, with applications including robotics, mapping, and sensor networks.
records.learning_note: Build the geometry skills used in planning and mapping. Feedback control then helps a robot follow a planned motion.
records.first_activity: Use a set of 2D points to represent obstacles and find the nearest point along a simulated route.

records.title: PySDR: Signals and frequency-domain practice
records.summary: An online guide to digital signal processing and software-defined radio in Python, with topics including sampling, Fourier transforms, and filtering.
records.first_activity: Generate a waveform in Python and compare its time and frequency plots. Use the simulation examples if you have no radio hardware.

records.title: DC Motor Speed: PID Controller Design
records.summary: A MATLAB tutorial that models DC motor speed and compares the step responses of proportional and PID controllers.
records.first_activity: Compare the tutorial's step-response plots and identify how much the speed overshoots and how long it takes to settle.

records.title: Signals & Communications
records.summary: Use signal and communications coursework to explore digital signal processing, radio frequency engineering, and wireless systems. Software-defined radio and open radio networks give students areas to explore.

records.title: Controls & Robotics
records.summary: Use modeling, feedback, and stability analysis to explore robotics, controls, and industrial automation. Mobile robots and manufacturing systems provide examples of these techniques in use.

records.title: Digital VLSI Systems Design
records.summary: Study the design, timing, analysis, and physical layout of digital CMOS circuits, from transistors and logic gates to sequential circuits and data paths.
records.learning_note: Connect digital logic to circuit-level tradeoffs in delay, noise margins, and layout.
records.first_activity: Compare two CMOS logic implementations and explain how gate capacitance can affect propagation delay.

records.title: Computer Architecture and Design
records.summary: Examines processor, memory, and interconnect organization, including pipelining, caches, multicore systems, and architectural design tradeoffs.
records.learning_note: Follow chip design into processor architecture and performance tradeoffs.
records.first_activity: Trace two instructions through a simple processor pipeline and identify a source of stalls.

records.title: Semiconductor Processing
records.summary: Surveys semiconductor fabrication steps, from wafer preparation through patterning, doping, etching, and metallization.
records.learning_note: Connect semiconductor device concepts to the steps and equipment used in a fabrication facility.
records.first_activity: Sketch a simple fabrication sequence and identify one purpose and one measurement for each step.

records.title: Quality Engineering
records.summary: Applies statistical process control, process capability analysis, and designed experiments to manufacturing and quality improvement.
records.learning_note: Use control charts and capability measures to investigate process variability and yield. The course page recommends SIE 305.
records.first_activity: Compare two simulated manufacturing lots using a control chart and explain which one warrants investigation.

records.title: Physical Properties of Materials
records.summary: Introduces solid-state explanations for materials' thermal, electrical, optical, and magnetic behavior.
records.learning_note: Build materials background for device physics. The course page lists MSE 222 or MSE 223R, concurrent OPTI 240, or department consent.
records.first_activity: Compare materials with different electrical and thermal properties and explain how the differences affect a device.

records.title: Verilator Create-Binary Example
records.summary: The Verilator project demonstrates compiling a small SystemVerilog design and running it as a standalone simulation.
records.first_activity: Use the example build flow to simulate a four-bit counter. Check reset, counting, and rollover.

records.title: Semiconductors & Digital Hardware
records.summary: Digital hardware designers and verification engineers build and test logic. Fabrication, process equipment, product testing, and advanced packaging are related areas with different learning routes.
